label: 2026 Q3
asOf: prices as of the 23 Oct 2026 close
headline: Ads sell at ever higher prices, but AI spending has eaten cash flow down to negative

points.t: Revenue +26%, average price per ad +14%, and Q4 guidance above expectations.

points.b: Profit held down by a one-off
points.t: A $9.9B legal settlement; excluding it, operating income +11% and EPS $7.40.

points.b: Cash flow negative for the first time
points.t: Quarterly capex of $34.9B exceeded operating cash flow; no 2027 budget given.

reaction: Stock: up about 1% after hours, then −7.0% the next day ($697.52 → $648.85), its biggest one-day drop in three months. It wasn't the results but the spending: negative free cash flow, a higher capex floor, and worries about financing and dilution from new non-voting Class C shares; the Nasdaq also fell 2.3% that day. Expectations are publicly reported consensus (Investing.com, investingLive); GAAP EPS consensus already included the legal costs.

volprice.title: Ad revenue = impressions × price
volprice.take: This quarter's growth came mainly from price: impression growth slowed from 19% early in the year to 10%, while average price per ad accelerated to +14%; ads work better, so advertisers pay more.
volprice.note: Meta only discloses growth rates, not absolute impressions or prices. 1.10 × 1.14 ≈ 1.25, consistent with +26% ad revenue. Daily active people 3.64B, +3% y/y.

segments.title: By segment
segments.take: Growth came almost entirely from the Family of Apps (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger); Reality Labs revenue is still shrinking.

rows.why: Operating income $17.1B, −31% y/y, mainly from the legal settlement. Company-wide operating income excluding it was +11%.
A $4.13B loss, 7% smaller than a year ago. Quest sales fell while AI glasses grew.

segments.note: The small chart shows Reality Labs' quarterly operating loss. Management said 2027 investment will shift from Reality Labs to AI.

extras.title: Signs of AI payback
extras.take: Ads are already seeing returns; new AI products are still in the spending phase.

items.w: Partnership ads run above $15B annualized, +97% y/y; nearly 10M advertisers have used at least one generative AI creative tool.
About 6 weeks after launch, more than 10M people in the US and Canada signed up and about 25% use it daily. Free for now; no numbers yet on monetization (commissions, subscriptions).
66,775 employees, −15% y/y (about 8,000 laid off in May). The labor savings are far from enough to cover compute and depreciation.
Management admitted Muse is compute-hungry, and costs rise with users; the goal is a 10x+ efficiency gain within a year, with no per-user cost given.

trends.why: Still growing; Q4 guided at a $74.5B midpoint
About 35% excluding one-offs, still 5 points below last year
Negative in Q3, a first in recent years

valuation.take: About 22x trailing earnings, below its five-year median of 24x. At the median multiple, the current price only needs a 2027 operating margin of about 26% (about 36% this year excluding one-offs): the market is pricing depreciation eating into margins, not paying a premium for ad growth.

forward.title: Full-year earnings from company guidance
steps: Q4 revenue at the guided midpoint of $74.5B
Full-year expense guide midpoint $177B less $127.1B in three quarters → Q4 expenses about $49.9B
Q4 operating income about $24.6B (33% margin), non-operating items at 0, tax at the 16% guided midpoint → net income about $20.6B
÷ 2.573B shares → Q4 EPS about $8.02 (public consensus about $8.26)
forward.note: Q4 annualized, the P/E is about 20x. Q1 included an $8.0B tax benefit and Q3 $9.9B of legal costs, which roughly offset. Our estimate, not a company forecast.

scenarios.title: Three scenarios: where the price sits
head: Case
Revenue growth

scenarios.note: Margin is the operating margin. Base: full-year 2026 revenue of about $256B (including the Q4 guided midpoint), 16% tax, 2.573B shares. *Price: if the market pays the five-year median of 24.2x, the current price needs 2027 EPS of $26.60; with 20% revenue growth that means an operating margin of only about 26.5%. The price sits between the bear and base cases, closer to the bear. After the January 2027 split, per-share numbers halve and multiples stay the same. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

history.title: Against its own last 5 years
history.note: About 22x now, above only 6 of the last 20 quarter ends, the 30th percentile; median about 24x. It was lower in 2022 (peak metaverse losses, ad growth turning negative) and in the first half of this year. The 31.5x at the end of September 2025 was inflated by a one-off tax item and doesn't mean it was really more expensive then. StockAnalysis data.

decomp.title: The −7.0% post-report move, decomposed
head: Measure
TTM earnings
P/E
decomp.note: The extra 10% of GAAP earnings is mainly last Q3's $15.9B tax charge dropping out of the trailing four quarters, not real extra profit. Excluding one-offs, earnings barely moved, so almost all of the drop was multiple compression: the market is discounting a bigger spending plan.

cash.title: Capex intensity
cash.note: Of every $100 of revenue, $54 goes into data centers, versus $38 a year ago. Cash and marketable securities of $82.5B now roughly equal long-term debt of $80.9B; no buybacks this quarter. The full-year capex guide implies $49–59B in Q4.

calc: Price $642.62: 23 Oct close; market cap $1,643B (StockAnalysis), about 2.556B shares
TTM free cash flow $14.08B + $12.39B + $0.78B − $2.12B = $25.1B; capex includes finance lease principal

Excluding one-offs: Q3'25 excluding the $15.9B tax charge is $7.25 (company disclosure); Q1'26 excluding the $8.03B tax benefit is about $7.31 ($18.74B ÷ 2.564B shares); Q3'26 excluding $9.9B of legal costs is $7.40 (company disclosure); Q2'26's $2.4B legal and $1.2B severance costs are not adjusted
Pre-report P/E: $697.52 ÷ $26.55 = 26.3x ($29.62 excluding one-offs → 23.5x); post-report: $648.85 ÷ $29.33 = 22.1x ($29.77 excluding → 21.8x)
Scenario EPS = 2027 revenue × operating margin × (1 − 16%) ÷ 2.573B shares

changes.before: 2026 at $130–145B; no 2027 number, only that plans aim to maximize 2026–2027 capacity.
changes.now: 2026 at $135–145B; still no 2027 number, only that it will keep “investing aggressively”, with guidance in January.
Expects “strong overall revenue growth” through 2027, with possible incremental revenue from new AI businesses.
2026 loss of $18–19B, narrowing to about $15B in 2027 as investment shifts to AI.

changes.before: More long-term debt, plus partnerships (such as the BlackRock data center) to share costs.
changes.now: New non-voting Class C shares, effectively a 2-for-1 split; stated uses include financing, employee pay and acquisitions, with no specific issuance plan yet.

items: About 6 weeks after launch, Muse has more than 10M sign-ups and about 25% use it daily
Annual revenue per existing user is “a few hundred dollars”; Muse would add commissions and subscriptions on top
Record time spent on Facebook and Instagram, mainly from video
Muse comes to Meta glasses next month
2027 expenses and capex: deferred to January
Muse serving cost per user: only listed cost-cutting levers, no number
When Muse makes money and how much: no numbers
Whether Class C shares will be used for financing soon: no specific plan
Whether free cash flow turns positive again
Price-per-ad growth drops back to single digits: the AI ad-performance gains are fading
2027 expense growth clearly outpaces revenue growth without matching new revenue
Muse user growth stalls, or serving costs don't fall
New large verdicts in teen-related lawsuits
